biography: Frédéric Vervisch, a name synonymous with flamboyant precision on the track, hails from the historic town of Roeselare, Belgium. His entry into motorsport was almost accidental. At the age of 14, while accompanying his father to a local karting event, Frédéric was dared to try a few laps. The seed was planted. He honed his skills in various karting series, often drawing attention for his aggressive overtaking maneuvers and a penchant for the dramatic. A defining moment came during the 2008 Formula Ford Benelux season where, despite a mechanical failure in the final race, his sheer determination in the preceding rounds earned him enough points to secure the championship. This victory catapulted him into the world of touring car racing. Now a veteran at 38, Vervisch finds himself as a key driver for the Goodwood Green team, a team known for its unconventional strategies and equally unconventional drivers. While he may not consistently be at the very front, his experience and showmanship make him a valuable asset and a fan favorite.
drivingStyle: Vervisch's driving style can be best described as 'calculated chaos'. He's not afraid to push the limits, often braking later and carrying more speed through corners than his competitors deem sensible. This aggressive approach, while thrilling to watch, can sometimes lead to costly mistakes. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he tends to favor early pace over long-term consistency. However, when under pressure, Vervisch possesses a remarkable ability to extract maximum performance from his car, often pulling off stunning overtakes in the closing laps of a race.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at the 2016 Macau Grand Prix, where Rossi accused Vervisch of deliberately blocking him during qualifying.
A fierce on-track battle for position during the 2021 Spa 24 Hours that resulted in multiple collisions and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.
A clash of egos. Both drivers are known for their flamboyant personalities and competitive spirit, leading to frequent clashes both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears a pair of lucky socks knitted by his grandmother before every race.
Insists on listening to a specific classical music piece – Bach's 'Toccata and Fugue in D minor' – immediately before putting on his helmet.
Has a peculiar habit of tracing the outline of the track on his steering wheel with his index finger during the formation lap.
famousQuote: Risk is just opportunity wearing a different outfit. You gotta be willing to see it, and then you gotta floor it.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2019 FIA WTCR Race of Germany at the Nürburgring Nordschleife after starting from 15th on the grid, showcasing his overtaking prowess and exceptional car control in treacherous conditions.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2017 TCR International Series finale in Dubai due to a mechanical failure, costing him the championship.
